title: The Bittern and the Hoopoe
summary: In ancient times, before they took their avian forms, the Bittern and the Hoopoe were mortal herdsmen pasturing cattle in adjacent meadows....
full_text:
In ancient times, before they took their avian forms, the Bittern and the Hoopoe were mortal herdsmen pasturing cattle in adjacent meadows.

The man who became the Bittern had rich, fat cows, but he was indolent and loved his afternoon nap. While he slumbered beneath the alders, his cows strayed into treacherous bogs and sank into the mire. When he awoke and found his herd missing, he rushed wildly among the reeds, crying in desperate mournful tones, "Come back! Come back!" transformed into a marsh bird whose hollow, booming cry echoes across the fens to this day.

The man who became the Hoopoe, on the other hand, was assigned lean, unruly heifers that sprinted in all directions. He had to run up hills and down valleys, waving his staff, shouting and whistling until his breath gave out: "Up, up, up! Heifers, back!" In the end, he was changed into the crested Hoopoe, whose distinctive call "Up-up-up" still sounds from sunny glades, forever echoing the frantic cries of a herdsman trying to keep his wandering herd in line.
moral: Neglect of duty brings lamentation, while diligent care preserves honor.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Bittern and the Hoopoe"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
